articles.title: Douglas County Easter Events Roundup: More Hunts Added, More On The Way

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: City of Roseburg Fire Department will begin issuing residential burn permits April 15. Permits cost $75, last seven days and are available through May 15. Only yard waste may be burned. Full permit details and request form: roseburgor.gov/departments/fire/burn-permits.
articles.title: City Of Roseburg Fire Department To Begin Issuing Residential Burn Permits April 15

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: The Glide Wildflower Show returns April 25-26 at the Glide Community Center with more than 400 species of native plants on display, guided walks, botanists, special presentations, plant sales, food and homemade pies.
articles.title: Glide Wildflower Show Returns April 25-26 With Native Plant Displays, Guided Walks and More

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Pacific Power customers in Oregon will see higher electric bills beginning April 1 after regulators approved a new rate adjustment. Most residential customers are expected to pay more each month, with the increase tied to higher power supply and related costs.
articles.title: PacifiCorp Customers In Oregon To See Rate Increase Beginning April 1

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Southern Oregon nonprofit leaders will gather in Roseburg on April 8-9 for the third annual Southern Oregon Nonprofit Summit at Aviva Health, featuring sessions on governance, advocacy, leadership, event planning and fundraising.
articles.title: Southern Oregon Nonprofit Summit Returns To Roseburg April 8-9

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Roseburg police reported multiple arrests and citations Tuesday, including warrant cases, several trespass incidents, a parole detainer, and a probation violation tied to reported drug use and disorderly behavior.
articles.title: Police Log: March 31, 2026

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Heavy snow and strong winds are expected above 3,000 feet in eastern Douglas County and the southern Oregon Cascades from Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. Forecasters say travel may become very difficult or impossible, especially near Crater Lake, Diamond Lake and along mountain passes.
articles.title: Winter Storm Warning Issued For High Elevations In Eastern Douglas County, Southern Oregon Cascades

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Music on the Half Shell says unaccompanied minors will be allowed at Tuesday night concerts during the 2026 season, reversing last year’s restriction. Organizers said the rule could be reinstated if problems involving unsupervised youth arise again.
articles.title: Music On The Half Shell To Allow Unaccompanied Minors At 2026 Concerts

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Free wildfire preparedness webinar set for May 6. The online event will cover home preparation, evacuation planning, wildfire risk reduction, local resources and burn restrictions, with speakers from the sheriff’s office, OSFM, DFPA and OSU Extension.
articles.title: Free Wildfire Safety Webinar Set For May 6

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Roseburg’s Brown Park is being transformed into a larger, inclusive playground for children of all abilities. The $1.1 million project will more than double the park’s size and add modern accessible features, with completion expected by late spring or early summer.
articles.title: Brown Park Expansion In Roseburg Aims To Create Inclusive Play Space For All Abilities

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Oregon emergency officials will host a free online webinar April 22 focused on helping rural communities prepare for disasters like wildfires, floods, ice storms and extreme heat. Registration is required, and interpretation plus captioning will be available.
articles.title: Oregon Emergency Management To Host Rural Disaster Preparedness Webinar Series

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Roseburg ODHS will host its monthly First Thursday community resource event from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. April 2 at 738 W. Harvard Ave. in Roseburg, bringing together 27 agencies and services including housing help, food boxes, clothing, showers, a mobile medical clinic and a free meal.
articles.title: Roseburg ODHS To Host Community Resource Event April 2

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: The new Golf Oregon specialty plate will be available through Oregon DMV starting April 28. The plate carries a $40 surcharge, with about $35 supporting the Junior Golf Fund. Applications will be accepted by mail, at DMV offices, through dealers and online for some transactions.
articles.title: Golf Oregon Specialty Plate Coming To Oregon DMV April 28

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Roseburg police reported 10 incidents Monday and early Tuesday, including multiple warrant arrests, a disorderly conduct arrest, a DUII crash, a trespass at WinCo, a littering arrest at T Mart, and citations for drug possession, inhalants and prohibited camping.
articles.title: Police Log: March 30, 2026

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Redbarn Dispensary has opened at 161 N. Main St., becoming the first marijuana dispensary within Winston city limits. The opening follows Winston’s 2025 ordinance change allowing recreational marijuana facilities after years of local debate.
articles.title: Redbarn Opens Winston’s First Dispensary Within City Limits; Grand Opening Near

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: Roseburg Public Library is asking the community to help shape its 2026 Summer Reading Program. Residents can take the “2026 SRP Survey” at RoseburgPublicLibrary.org, email feedback, or pick up a paper copy at the library. Responses are due by Saturday, April 11.
articles.title: Roseburg Library Seeks Community Input As Summer Reading Plans Take Shape

articles.author: Joseph Ziegler
articles.description: The Oregon 42 improvement project in Winston is continuing, with ODOT announcing overnight road work through early April. Drivers should expect intermittent lane closures at night as crews complete utility adjustments and pavement repairs.
articles.title: ODOT: Oregon 42 Project In Winston Continues With Night Work In Early April

articles.description: Adapt Integrated Health Care honored Q1 2026 employees with a March 19 recognition luncheon celebrating 110 combined years of service. Leaders praised the honorees’ dedication, compassion and long-term impact on the organization and the communities it serves.

articles.description: Roseburg police reported a busy March 27-29 with multiple DUII arrests, thefts, trespass cases, warrants, parole and probation violations, a hit-and-run arrest, and a strangulation case, according to the latest City of Roseburg police log.

articles.description: Umpqua National Forest and the National Forest Foundation planted 429,500 seedlings across 2,255 acres this winter, including helicopter-supported planting in hard-to-reach areas burned by the Jack, Little Bend, Chaos and Archie Creek fires.
articles.title: Umpqua National Forest, National Forest Foundation Plant 429,500 Seedlings Across Burn Areas
